surprises.head: Edmonton couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: Detroit usually allows more dangerous shots than most teams. Not tonight: Edmonton’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 3.9% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.3% (about 6.6% against Detroit) and a league average of 6.4%. A team strays this far about once every 100 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

story.head: A first NHL win for Postava
paras: Vasily Podkolzin got the scoring started for the Oilers early in the first. The Oilers’ Zach Hyman left in the second period and didn’t return. Two days later, he was placed on injured reserve with an upper-body injury. Viktor Arvidsson made it 1-1 for Detroit on the power play midway through the period. The third period was a wild one. Isaac Howard put the Oil back ahead 2-1 on the power play early in the period, but Emmitt Finnie tied it 2-2 for Detroit 30 seconds later. Colton Dach restored the Oilers’ lead with three and a half minutes left. With the goalie pulled and a little over a minute left, Dylan Larkin tied it up for Detroit. Lucas Raymond scored the only goal of the shootout for the Red Wings.

The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. The Oilers hit two posts and still lost. Michal Postava got his first NHL win, making 24 saves in his first NHL start. Tristan Jarry stopped 25 of 28 for the Oilers. By our Swing measure, Evan Bouchard had the best night of anyone, even in a loss. The Red Wings improved to 5-4-3, seventh in the Atlantic, while the Oilers fell to 8-2-2, still first in the Pacific.
